title: Nike Vomero 19 and Vaporfly 5 Deliver Innovation for Everyday Miles and Race-Day Performance
summary: Nike Running is unveiling two new footwear models built to fuel the runner journey: Vomero 19, a maximum cushioned daily trainer designed for everyday miles and the moments in between, and Nike Vaporfly 5, engineered for pinnacle race-day performance.
body_markdown:
Every runner’s journey is built step by step. It starts with a goal, continues through the daily miles, and comes together on race day, when preparation turns into possibility.


Nike Running is unveiling two new footwear models built to fuel that journey: Vomero 19, a maximum cushioned daily trainer designed for everyday miles and the moments in between, and Nike Vaporfly 5, engineered for pinnacle race-day performance.


Together, the silhouettes reflect Nike’s commitment to helping runners move forward, from their first steps out the door to the final push through the finish line. One shoe helps the everyday miles feel just that much better. The other makes runners feel light, fast and ready to push for more.


**The Trusted Vomero Feel, Made Better**


Race-day possibility is built on the miles that come before it: the recovery runs, everyday miles and longer efforts that help runners create consistency and prepare for what’s next.


Vomero 19 is made for those moments. Nike’s icon of maximum cushioning delivers the comfort and impact protection runners depend on, balancing softness, responsiveness and support to help make everyday miles feel easier.


The latest Vomero represents an evolution, not a revolution. It preserves the maximum cushioning, stability and familiar geometry of[its predecessor](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-vomero-18-official-images) while focusing updates where runners asked for them most: lighter weight and greater breathability.


A plush layer of responsive ZoomX foam pairs with a new, lightweight ReactX LT midsole compound to deliver a balanced combination of cushioning, bounce and energy return.


Up top, a seamless engineered mesh construction provides a softer, lighter and more breathable fit from the first step. A redesigned tongue and heel add cushioning and support where runners need it, while a new radial outsole improves traction and contributes to a smoother, more stable ride.


Together, these updates create a maximum cushioned daily trainer that’s lighter than Vomero 18 while maintaining its stack height, comfort and trusted underfoot feel.


Because for runners logging consistent miles, comfort isn’t an indulgence. It’s what helps them recover from harder efforts, keep doing more of what they love, and get after it again tomorrow.


“The best running shoes become more than just something you run in. They’re the pair you reach for without thinking,” says Ashley Campbell, Nike Running Footwear Product Manager. “That’s the feeling we wanted to protect with Vomero 19: something familiar, comfortable and dependable that’s there for you, whatever the day or the run brings.”


**The Most Aggressive Vaporfly Yet**


From the 5K to the half-marathon, Vaporfly 5 is built for runners who want to attack the pace from start to finish, with the confidence to pursue a breakthrough performance or a new personal best.


As the latest addition to[Nike’s race-day system of speed](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-debuts-a-race-day-system-of-speed-designed-for-every-runner) , the new Vaporfly sharpens that chase with a ride that’s light, fast and more aggressive than ever before. Fine-tuned through athlete insight,[Nike Sport Research Lab](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/lebron-james-innovation-center-nike-sport-research-lab) testing and racing innovation, the silhouette pairs a redesigned Flyplate with two proprietary foams and targeted traction underfoot. Together, the elements work as one system to deliver a lightweight, responsive ride that makes runners feel as fast as they look.


“Nearly a decade after Vaporfly[changed the conversation around race-day footwear](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/a-decade-of-the-super-shoe-how-nike-redefined-speed) , we’re still inspired by the same question: How can we help athletes unlock more speed?” says Natasha Lewis, Director, Nike Racing Footwear. “Vaporfly 5 is about that moment when everything comes together and you feel light, fast and ready to push for more. That’s the feeling we want runners to have with every step.”


At the center of Vaporfly 5 is a new, wave-shaped Flyplate. A ripple through the midfoot creates a spring-like sensation under the arch, while a wider midfoot provides added stability and an extended tip supports a quick, propulsive toe-off.


The Flyplate works in unison with a pair of performance foams engineered to function as one system. Standard ZoomX sits below the plate for familiar bounce and responsiveness, while new ZoomX LT is layered above the plate, delivering race-specific cushioning without unnecessary weight. The new foam is 17 percent lighter than ZoomX and offers 8 percent more energy return.


Together, the plate and foams create a more energetic, unconstrained sensation underfoot, bringing together cushioning, bounce and propulsion in a ride that feels light, fast and aggressive.


That system sits within a bold new stance and silhouette that makes Vaporfly 5 as visually striking as it is fast, with an unmistakable design that signals its performance before the race even starts — featuring added cushioning underfoot while maintaining[its predecessor](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/vaporfly-4-streakfly-2-official-images) ’s heel-to-toe offset.


Weight reductions in targeted areas help balance the additional cushioning with a noticeably lightweight feel. Simplicity guided each design decision, allowing every part of the shoe to contribute to the feeling of speed.


A soft and breathable Vapor Mesh upper uses a fully engineered, seamless construction to create a sock-like fit. A reductive tongue adds containment and comfort, and a molded ZoomX sock liner helps runners feel secure as the pace increases.


Meanwhile, a thin GOATEK rubber outsole adds targeted traction in the forefoot, giving runners the grip they need for race-day speed while reducing unnecessary material.


“The shoe is still cushioned and forgiving, but it’s also very responsive through the new carbon plate,” says Nike athlete Mohammed Ahmed, an Olympic silver medalist in the 5,000 meter. “You can feel both elements working together, creating a smooth and comfortable ride while remaining controlled and secure underfoot.”


Vaporfly 5 is currently a prototype. The final product will be available in fall 2027.


Vomero 19 will be available in March 2027 at[nike.com](https://www.nike.com/) and select retail locations.


Nike will also continue to expand its road running footwear lineup in 2027 with the introduction of Pegasus Fly, a new entry point into the iconic Pegasus franchise with a lighter, more connected way to experience everyday speed.
